title: AMR canonical event envelope 2.0
description:
Removes state_code and district_code. Those two fields encoded one country's administrative hierarchy in the wire format itself: a country with three sub-national levels could not express the third, and a country with one had to leave a field called 'district' empty forever. 2.0 carries country_code plus the administrative chain, which describes any country's hierarchy without naming any country's levels.

This is a breaking change and it is meant to be. 1.0 and 1.1 are withdrawn; a producer on either must move to 2.0. Migration is mechanical: state_code becomes admin_codes[level 1].code and district_code becomes admin_codes[level 2].code.

country_code.description: ISO 3166-1 alpha-3. Without it an event cannot be placed once more than one country reports.

admin_codes.description: The administrative chain, outermost first. Levels are numbered, never named, so the same envelope carries a two-level country and a five-level one. An event that is national or aggregate carries none, which is why this is not required.

code_system.description: Authority for the code at this level — ISO3166-2, GeoNames, or a national scheme. Stated per level because a country may draw its levels from different authorities.

admin_path.description: Materialised path of codes, e.g. IND/28/583. Redundant with admin_codes; carried so a consumer can filter by prefix without reassembling it.

reporting_period.description: How the event's period was derived. Epidemiological weeks differ between systems, so the system used is stated rather than assumed.

timezone.description: IANA zone the observation was recorded in. Set where a country spans several, since a country-level default mis-stamps day boundaries.
